root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking something away by light, sudden snatching.
root_idea.development: Its lexical extensions include forcible deprivation and spoil, removal of coverings such as bark, and specialized usages connected with bereavement, speed, and way or manner.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested Form I verb and is presented under the normalized perfect citation form سَلَبَ.

senses.definition: To seize, snatch away, or deprive someone of something by force.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive verb used with the person from whom something is taken and the thing taken, as in سَلَبَهُ الشَّيْءَ and سَلَبَهُ ثَوْبَهُ. The Quranic usage describes something being snatched away from people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deprive someone of reason or understanding; bereft of reason.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to a person or to the mind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To peel or strip a cane or reed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested as an imperative construction applied to a cane or reed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Privation or deprivation in a general technical sense; in grammar and logic, negation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical usage contrasted with affirmation or positive assertion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light, rapid travelling or journeying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun usage describing movement performed lightly and quickly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on black garments and observe mourning for a deceased husband, loved one, or other dead person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mourning practice may be for a husband or, in the broader usage, for another beloved or close relation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with another, each trying to seize or carry off something by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction describing mutual competition or struggle over an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a female animal or woman: bereaved of her young because it died, was lost or taken, or was cast in an imperfect state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly applied to a she-camel and she-gazelle, and also extended to a woman; the derived adjectives describe the bereaved female.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a tree or palm: stripped or bare of its leaves, branches, or fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes trees without leaves and palms without fruit; the adjective describes vegetation from which its covering or produce has been removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the panic grass: to put forth its leaves and become ready to be cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage applied to the plant called الثُّمَامُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The longest part of a plough's apparatus, or a wooden piece joined to the ploughshare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical agricultural term for a structural part of the plough.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Spoil, plunder, or booty seized from an opponent, including what is upon him or with him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May include clothing, weapons, and the mount of a defeated person; the plural is أَسْلَابٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hide, shanks, and paunch of a slaughtered animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for parts of a slaughtered animal, traditionally associated with what is allotted as spoil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The peel, rind, or bark of a cane, reed, or certain trees, including fibrous material used for ropes or baskets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote the bark itself or the fibrous plant material obtained from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light, active, agile, or quick in movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, bull, or horse, especially with reference to the hands, legs, or movement in thrusting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long or tall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied, among other things, to a spear or a man; this is a distinct adjectival usage from agility or quickness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The denuded or unclad part of the body; nudity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing a state or visible condition of being unclad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A string or cord tied to a camel's muzzle, distinct from its halter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term for a particular camel cord.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sinew bound around an arrow, especially along the reed or cane shaft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical archery term for the sinew fastening on an arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Black garments or a black cloth worn by a woman in mourning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The garment may be associated with mourning a husband, child, or another beloved person; the sources record variation in number and lexical analysis.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spear that takes away life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet for a deadly spear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man or woman who habitually or repeatedly spoils or plunders people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intensive epithets describing repeated or excessive plundering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller or maker of ropes or baskets made from سَلَب material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A professional designation derived from the plant material called سَلَبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A row or line of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal usage recorded as an early sense of the word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road, way, course, mode, manner, kind, or style.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a physical route and for a manner of acting, conducting oneself, or speaking; the plural is أَسَالِيبُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, an elevated or fixed nose expressing pride.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Derived from the expression of looking in one direction without turning right or left.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The aperture of a watering trough or tank through which water flows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term for the water outlet of the trough or tank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The neck of a lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A game or customary performance of the desert Arabs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer either to the game itself or to an action performed within the group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go at a very quick pace or move so swiftly as if emerging from one's skin; to outstrip others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially applied to a horse or camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unfamiliar, unsociable, ungentle, or not inclined toward anyone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative characterization of a person likened to a wild animal.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is an imperfect active Form I form, يَسْلُبْ; the public headword is normalized to the perfect citation form سَلَبَ.
